name: National Syndicalism
summary: National syndicalism fuses revolutionary syndicalism with integral nationalism: workers are to be won from Marxist internationalism into a nation-state organized as a vertical syndicate of producers, with class struggle replaced by collaboration under state direction. It rejects liberal democracy, parties and parliaments, capitalism and Marxism alike, and values will, discipline, direct action and imperial national destiny.
scope: Mainly the Spanish strand of 1931-37: Ledesma Ramos's La Conquista del Estado and JONS, Onésimo Redondo, and the 1934 program of FE de las JONS under José Antonio Primo de Rivera, with the Italian precursors (Sorel's syndicalism, Corradini, Panunzio, Rossoni) as background. It excludes Franco's later Francoist regime, the anarcho-syndicalist CNT, and non-Spanish fascism generally.

keyFigures.name: Ramiro Ledesma Ramos
keyFigures.role: Founder of La Conquista del Estado and the JONS, and the main theorist of Spanish national syndicalism

keyFigures.name: José Antonio Primo de Rivera
keyFigures.role: Founder of Falange Española and author of its 1934 program

keyFigures.name: Onésimo Redondo
keyFigures.role: Leader of the Juntas Castellanas that merged into the JONS in 1931

sources.title: Programa de la Falange Española de las JONS (1934), 26/27-point program as published in ABC, 30 Nov 1934
sources.author: José Antonio Primo de Rivera / FE de las JONS (hosted by Universitat de València)
sources.usedFor: Primary text of the national-syndicalist program: nation and empire, totalitarian state, abolition of parties, vertical syndicates, rejection of capitalism and Marxism, banking, land, Catholicism, national revolution.

sources.usedFor: Ledesma's La Conquista del Estado and the JONS, statism, syndicalist economy, his atheism and view of the Church.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The program rejects capitalism and has the state intervene in economic conflict instead of standing aside, organizing the economy as one syndicate of producers (points 9-11).

public-ownership.rationale: Point 14 favors nationalizing banking and running major public services through corporations, though most industry stays in private hands.

unions-good.rationale: The movement organized unions itself (JONS built Castilian unions) and makes syndicates the economic base, but as state-integrated bodies rather than independent ones.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is legitimate only as a means to individual, family and social ends (point 13), and the program allows nationalized banking and uncompensated expropriation of illegitimately held land.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state is to shield the economy from big financial capital and speculators and bind producers into corporations under national direction (points 11, 13).

cut-welfare.rationale: The program keeps and expands social legislation and supports the involuntarily unemployed (point 15), though it scorns those who live off others' work.

worker-ownership.rationale: Syndicates join employers and workers vertically and private initiative serving the collective is kept (points 8-9); there is no program of worker takeover.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No concept of protected groups; speech is limited only by national discipline (point 7), so adherents would not endorse hate-speech laws as such.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement sought a nationalist dictatorship and unified under a single Jefe Nacional in 1934.

state-harmful.rationale: Point 6 makes the state a totalitarian instrument of national integrity, the opposite of anti-statism.

empower-police-military.rationale: Point 4 demands armed forces as large as needed for independence and world standing, with public dignity for the military.

decide-locally.rationale: Separatism is a crime and Spain is one unity of destiny (point 2); local bodies only serve as channels of participation within the national state (point 6).

traditional-family.rationale: The family is named as a basic unit of participation (point 6) and the program aims at family landholdings (point 19), in a Catholic framework.

more-religion-public.rationale: Catholicism is part of the national identity, but the state is placed above the Church and Ledesma was an atheist, so support is moderate.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: National unity and pride through education and a Hispanic cultural mission are central (points 3, 23).

gradual-change.rationale: Point 26 calls for a new order by national revolution against the resistance of the existing one.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Point 3 rejects foreign domination and seeks Spanish imperial standing, which cuts against supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: The program calls for protective tariffs (point 18) and a nationally directed economy.

nation-first.rationale: Individual, group and class interests must yield to the supreme reality of the nation (point 1).

open-borders.rationale: The nation as a unity of destiny with strict discipline (points 2, 7) is incompatible with open borders.

revolution-justified.rationale: The program is explicitly revolutionary: a national revolution, direct, ardent and combative (point 26).

experts-over-public.rationale: Blinkhorn describes the leader's vision as elitist regenerationism, implying rule by an elite rather than popular opinion.

central-planning.rationale: The state directs the economy through syndicates and nationalized credit but keeps private initiative (point 8), so adherents would not claim full central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not the model; the program's mixed syndicate structure has private enterprise under state direction, not worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not in the program; land reform proceeds by redistribution and expropriation instead (points 19, 21).

basic-income.rationale: Contradicts the duty to work and contempt for those who live off others (point 16).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Point 18 explicitly lists protective tariffs for agriculture; extension to industry follows from the national economy aim.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state does not stand aside from economic conflict and nationalizes banking and credit (points 11, 14).

widespread-small-property.rationale: Point 18-19 aim to consolidate farms and create family holdings, ending both wasteful large estates and uneconomic smallholdings, and protecting property from financial capital.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The program keeps private property, private initiative and a right to work in a producers' economy, and rejects Marxism (points 8, 10).

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The program wants banking nationalized (point 14), the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Point 9 organizes the whole economy into vertical syndicates of employers and workers by branch of production.

one-party-rule.rationale: Parties are to be abolished in favour of a nationalist dictatorship led by the movement; the Falange later became the single party of Franco's state.

democracy-best.rationale: Point 6 abolishes parties, inorganic suffrage and conventional parliaments.

direct-votes.rationale: Point 6 rejects inorganic suffrage; participation is through family, municipality and syndicate.

workers-councils.rationale: Syndicates are vertical, state-integrated and include employers, and political participation is by organic channels but within a totalitarian state, not councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Point 2 calls separatism a crime and would annul the Constitution for encouraging division.

natural-rulers.rationale: Blinkhorn describes the elitist regenerationism of the movement's leadership; a hierarchical leader principle presumes some are fitted to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Payne says the programme treated political violence as a means of national regeneration, and the party kept an armed wing.

war-builds-character.rationale: Point 26 views life as militancy and sacrifice and point 4 wants a military outlook to shape national life.

separate-church-state.rationale: Point 25 has Church and state coordinate and adopts Catholic tradition, though the state keeps its dignity; strict separation is not the aim.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The party rejected direct clerical influence in government and put the state above the Church.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A totalitarian state serving national integrity (point 6) and large national armed forces (point 4) exclude privatized security.

military-superiority.rationale: Point 4 wants armed forces large enough to guarantee world standing and point 3 seeks a leading role in Europe.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Spain is defined as a unity of destiny (point 2) and a Hispanic cultural community, not as an ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejects Marxism and aims to make class struggle impossible (points 10-11).

equal-outcomes.rationale: The program wants decent living for all (point 12) but within hierarchy; there is no equal-outcome goal.

civilizational-union.rationale: Point 3 seeks to unify culture, economic interests and power with Hispanic America.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Point 1 subordinates individual interests to the nation, and capitalism is rejected for ignoring popular needs (point 10).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual interests yield to the nation (point 1), freedom exists only within a strong nation (point 7), and all have a duty to work (point 16).

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Syndicalist national movements were productivist, favoring industrial labor, not rejecting industry.

restore-past-order.rationale: The program demands a new order by national revolution (point 26), not a restoration, and the movement rejected conservatives as much as the left.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is doctrinal and militant; adherents would not subordinate national-syndicalist principles to pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: Point 26 sets a direct, combative style, and national syndicalism descends from Sorelian direct action; parliaments are to be abolished.

means-match-ends.rationale: The disciplined, militant movement saw itself as a prototype of the disciplined national order it wanted (points 26-27).

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The economy is built on syndicates organized by branch of production (point 9).

distribute-by-need.rationale: Wealth should serve the whole people (point 12), but work and national contribution remain the basis (point 16).

production-for-use.rationale: Point 12 says wealth should improve the people's living conditions, though private initiative and profit are retained (point 8).

profit-exploitation.rationale: The program rejects Marxism and distinguishes legitimate productive enterprise from speculative finance (points 8, 10, 13).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marxism is rejected and class rule is replaced by a producers' syndicate under a national state (points 9-10).

collective-farming.rationale: Point 19 favors family holdings and farmers' unions, not collectivized agriculture.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Italian strand held that proletarian nations need imperialism against richer powers, but the program treats capitalism's flaw as misery, not war.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state directs economic life and national finance; the program has no anti-tax theme.

harm-principle.rationale: The state is totalitarian and freedom is subordinate to national discipline (points 6-7).

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individuals participate only through family, municipality and syndicate (point 6), and individual interests yield to the nation.

conscription.rationale: Point 23 gives all men pre-military training for the national army and point 20 allows mobilizing all youth.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The nation is a supreme reality and unity of destiny (points 1-2), and the movement rejects both voting and exit as checks.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a totalitarian instrument serving national integrity, not a firm serving customers (point 6).

positive-liberty.rationale: The right to work and material support for the unemployed (point 15) point toward a material view of freedom, though the program's own framing of freedom is national.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The program defines Spain by destiny and culture, not biology, and does not rest on racial science.

organic-representation.rationale: Point 6 has citizens take part through family, municipality and syndicate instead of parties.

total-state.rationale: Point 6 calls the state a totalitarian instrument, and education, culture and the economy are all state duties (points 9, 23).

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement aims at national revolution and regeneration from a decadent liberal order (points 1, 26).

territorial-expansion.rationale: Point 3 sets an imperial destiny, but Primo de Rivera described empire as cultural leadership over Hispanic America rather than conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The leader principle involves personal fidelity, but the movement conceived a modern totalitarian state, not feudal lord-vassal bonds.

bound-labor.rationale: The agrarian program aims at free family holdings and farmers' unions, not legally bound labor (point 19).

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Sorelian myth and vitalism point one way, Catholic natural-law tradition the other; adherents were split.

universal-morality.rationale: Human dignity and freedom are called eternal values (point 7) in a Catholic framework, but reason as the route to them is not stressed.

single-common-good.rationale: The nation is treated as one organic whole whose interest overrides class and sectional claims (points 1, 11).

workplace-democracy.rationale: The syndicates are hierarchical bodies integrated with the state and not run by workplace vote (points 9, 11).

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is an essential state duty meant to instill national unity (point 23).

economic-freedom.rationale: Freedom exists only within a strong nation (point 7) and capitalism is rejected (point 10).

rule-by-example.rationale: The movement emphasized service, sacrifice and elite leadership, but its program relies on discipline and punishment too.

national-self-determination.rationale: Spain's own unity and sovereignty are asserted (points 1-3), but nations within Spain are denied the same right.

reason-over-faith.rationale: National syndicalism built on Sorel's myth, vitalism and heroic action, which exalt will and emotion over reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Social protection is framed as a duty to Spaniards (point 15); no extension to foreigners is suggested.

work-for-welfare.rationale: All able-bodied Spaniards have a duty to work and idlers get no regard (point 16), though involuntary unemployment is supported (point 15).

class-collaboration.rationale: Point 11 treats all producers as one organic whole to make class struggle impossible.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The program stresses Hispanic tradition and Catholic heritage; it has no cult of destroying inherited institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Corradini's idea of a proletarian nation against wealthy powers supports such a front, but the Spanish program pursues Hispanic rather than wider fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: National syndicalism holds that workers belong to the nation, as with Corradini and Rossoni, and aims to draw them from Marxist internationalism into the national state (point 10).

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Sección Femenina was an auxiliary, nursing and support organization, implying separate roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Point 18 offers cheap national credit to end usury, which regulates interest rather than banning lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of the program, which defines the nation by destiny and Hispanic culture.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is above classes, an instrument of national integrity (point 6), and the program denies class struggle.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy theory unattested in the 1930s movement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Point 6 abolishes parties and parliaments, so any party-list system is rejected.

national-mission.rationale: Point 3 casts Spain as the spiritual center of the Hispanic world, a cultural mission more than export of a system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The party opposed oligarchy and the liberal party system it saw as divisive.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is totalitarian and actively directs the economy (points 6, 11, 14).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hispanidad celebrates a shared Hispanic community; no racial doctrine appears in the program.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The program calls dignity an eternal value (point 7) but sets rights below duties and builds a hierarchical state.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents see Spain's empire as a civilizing and spiritual achievement (point 3).

restrict-conversion.rationale: Falange did not seek to impose Catholicism on non-believers.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a concern of the movement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education should reflect Spain's Catholic tradition (point 25).

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy rests on national destiny and the movement's revolution, not on voters (points 2, 6, 26).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Payne notes the programme treated political violence as regeneration; adherents reject non-initiation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Sorelian and vitalist currents stress struggle and heroism, and imperial rivalry among nations (Corradini).

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom is conceived within the nation's discipline (point 7), not as protection from arbitrary power.

separated-powers.rationale: Abolishes parliaments and parties for a unitary totalitarian state (point 6).

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement saw itself as a disciplined elite winning through its own forces (point 27) but aimed to win workers to the nation, not lead them as a class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Point 12 says wealth must serve the people and mass misery is intolerable, though national interest outranks class.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The programme called for criminalizing strikes and lockouts; syndicates settle disputes under the state.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The program blames capitalism and an unjust landed order for misery (points 10, 18).

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rejects elections and parliaments for a hierarchical organic order led by the movement.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Point 7 provides strict discipline against anyone using freedom against the nation, and the movement saw itself in war with the existing order.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces get a dignified place in the national state (point 4) and not as a party arm.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Points 26-27 require discipline, militancy and a few pacts, with the movement winning only through its disciplined forces.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Point 3 rejects foreign domination and wants Spain to hold a leading role, not dissolve sovereignty.

clerical-rule.rationale: The party rejected direct clerical influence and put the state above the Church.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Internationalist defeatism is the Marxist stance it rejects; nation outranks class (points 1, 10).

recall-officials.rationale: Parliamentary-electoral mechanisms are rejected (point 6), so recall holds no appeal.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Point 3 rejects isolation and seeks a leading role in Europe and the world.

people-in-arms.rationale: The program wants large professional forces (point 4), plus pre-military training for all (point 23).

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The countryside is the permanent nursery of Spain (point 17) and a priority for rebuilding.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement attracted prominent intellectuals and valued higher education for the deserving (point 24).

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hispanic culture is cast as the spiritual center of a world mission (point 3), implying a hierarchy.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Adherents' stance unknown; Catholic tradition in schools and Ledesma's atheism pull in opposite directions.

minority-language-support.rationale: Separatism is a crime and Spain is one unity (point 2), so regional-language politics are discouraged.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state's integrity and discipline outrank group claims (points 6-7).

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Corradini's proletarian-nation idea supports poor nations' claims but the Spanish program is silent; adherents had no settled view.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Discipline and conformity to the national task come first (points 1, 7, 26).

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The program ties national independence to ending foreign and financial capital's dominance (points 3, 13).

constituent-assembly.rationale: Point 2 annuls the Constitution by revolution, not through an elected assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Freedom is subordinate to national strength and discipline (point 7).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: National interest comes first (point 1) and Spain pursues its own imperial standing.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Elections are rejected for an organic state with a Jefe Nacional.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banking is to be nationalized and put under national direction (point 14).

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Point 13 makes private property legitimate as a means to individual, family and social ends.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The movement rejected Marxism but had no developed analysis of the USSR.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The program wants the state to respect the Catholic tradition and keep church and state separate in function, but Ledesma's atheism and totalitarian statism pulled the other way, leaving adherents mildly against curbing the Church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The program abolishes parties and puts the national unit above them, so a head of state above party is consistent; the movement did not discuss the office as such.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The program declares the unity of the fatherland irrevocable and calls separatism a crime against Spain, which it would put down by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The program insists on the unity of destiny of Spain and rejects regional separatism, with one national syndicalist economic and legal order for all parts.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The movement was authoritarian and Catholic but not monarchist, and did not claim divine descent for its leader; a sacred ruler is foreign to its secular nationalism.

leader-cult.rationale: Falange built a cult of the Jefe and of Jose Antonio, with portraits, salutes and mass praise, as scholars note.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class struggle is rejected in favour of collaboration of producers in state-run vertical syndicates, so the premise that it should continue is refused.

land-redistribution.rationale: The program and its own recorded position call for expropriating idle or illegitimately held estates and settling family farmers.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hispanidad aims at a spiritual and political community of Hispanic peoples under Spanish leadership.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The program declares Spain an indivisible unit of destiny and treats separatism as an unforgivable crime.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: National syndicalism stresses will, spirit and national destiny over economic determinism and rejects Marxist materialism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Direct action and violence by committed minorities were central to its method, as scholars of the Falange and JONS document.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education is to instill national unity and pride as a state duty (point 23).

former-empire-influence.rationale: Point 3 casts Spain as the spiritual centre of the Hispanic world and claims an imperial destiny toward its former territories.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: All private interests are subordinated to the nation and state direction of the economy (points 1, 11), leaving no room for unlimited private discretion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The program rejects liberal constitutionalism and parliaments in favour of a totalitarian state (points 6-7), so entrenched limits on government are refused.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rejects party-based suffrage; the state is led by a Command, not elected rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: The nation-state absorbs individual and class interests in vertical syndicates under state direction, leaving no minority veto.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1934 program abolishes parties and parliament, and national syndicalism rejects liberal democracy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Point 27 says life is a militia of service and sacrifice, and national syndicalism stresses will, discipline and direct action.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: National syndicalism is a fascist current and rejects anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: It condemns Marxism but advocates a totalitarian state, so it rejects equating itself with communism.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: It rejects liberal parliamentary democracy as unsuited to Spain and proposes national syndicate-based institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Point 4 of the 1934 program restores public dignity to the armed forces and wants a military sense of life across Spain.

office-by-exam.rationale: Ledesma favored a technocratic, authoritarian state but no examination system is documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Point 14 nationalizes banking and public services, and national syndicalism favors economic nationalism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Point 6 abolishes parties and parliaments; delegates bound and recallable by constituents contradicts the authoritarian state.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliaments are abolished in point 6, so the executive does not need elected approval of its budget.

corporate-influence.rationale: National syndicalism rejects capitalism as well as Marxism and puts the economy under state-directed syndicates, so business domination of politics is opposed.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement rejects liberal democracy and glorifies national imperial will, so promoting democracy for peace is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: The program organises producers in vertical syndicates by industry, and Rossoni and Panunzio built syndicalism on this.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement prizes direct action and violence but through a disciplined party and national syndicates, not informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: Adherents split: Ledesma was an atheist who defined the nation without religion, while Redondo and Jose Antonio stressed Catholic tradition.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The program makes Spain a single totalitarian state and rejects separatism, so regional revenue retention is opposed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Production is organized in state-directed vertical syndicates with private property kept, not held in common.

defeat-communism.rationale: National syndicalism set out to win workers from Marxist internationalism and rejected Marxism as well as capitalism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Adherents split: Ledesma was an atheist hostile to Church influence while Redondo and the Falange stressed Catholicism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The program rejects capitalism as an exploitative system, so it is not praised as a progressive force.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The program is for a unitary totalitarian state with vertical syndicates, not self-governing communes.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The program and the doctrine reject both capitalism and Marxism and offer national syndicalism as the third course.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ledesma and the JONS wanted a single national state that crushes parties, and accepted violence.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Ledesma's JONS put the state above the Church while Redondo's wing was strongly Catholic, so adherents were split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: National syndicalism replaced parliamentary politics with state-led syndicates, not direct participation in decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The strand rejected class struggle and sought class harmony within the nation.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: National syndicalism claimed to transcend liberal capitalism and Marxism, combining nationalism with a social program.

social-market-economy.rationale: It sought a state-led syndicate economy, rejecting both liberal markets and Marxism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The program asserts the need for strong armed forces and imperial ambition.

property-franchise.rationale: It rejected liberal democracy and parliaments and proposed representation through syndicates, not a property franchise.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The strand rejected liberal parliamentarism and the party system in favor of a strong state and corporate representation, so lot-chosen assemblies are alien to it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The program rejects capitalism, nationalizes banking and expropriates idle landholdings, treating concentrated economic power as a threat to national and worker independence.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: National syndicalism wants a strong authoritarian state with discipline and direct action; abolishing police and prisons runs against it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Points 2 and 3 demand the unity of Spain and reject separatism, so guaranteed shares for communities are rejected.

vote-delegation.rationale: Point 6 abolishes parties and individual suffrage, replacing them with participation through family, municipality and syndicate.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Integral nationalism reserves political voice for the nation; the movement drew on FE de las JONS positions on citizenship.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The JONS and Falange used blue shirts, militias and drilled youth sections.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: National syndicalism organises everyone as producers in syndicates and rejects capitalism and rentier gains.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: National syndicalism prizes will, discipline and direct action and endorsed violence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The program asserts Spain as an irrevocable unity of destiny with an imperial historic mission.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Falangism held fixed gender roles in a patriarchal family and a Women's Section dedicated to domestic and service roles.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Falangism assigned women a fixed role through the Sección Femenina and had no feminist politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Falange's cult of "the Fallen" (Caidos), with José Antonio as its martyr, was central to its ritual.

culture-before-state.rationale: Ledesma's La Conquista del Estado puts conquest of the state first.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Patriarchal outlook and subordination of religion to the state, but not a feminist critique of it.

independent-unions.rationale: Syndicates were to be organised vertically under state direction, uniting workers and employers, and not as independent class bodies.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership was to be handled through the state and syndicates; Ledesma's programme was statist and gave no role to municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The program wants a totalitarian state with central authority, not delegates that only coordinate local assemblies.

person-over-state.rationale: Ledesma's La Conquista del Estado and the program make the totalitarian state the supreme end to which individuals are subordinate.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The program insists on the unity of Spain and opposes separatism, so regional powers rest on national authority.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement defined the nation by destiny and culture, not race, and rejected organising by group interest against national unity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The program declares a will to Empire and national expansion, not defence alone.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1934 program replaces parties and inorganic suffrage with family, municipal and syndical participation, which excludes separate religious electorates.

arms-reduction.rationale: The program demands a strong army, navy and air force, and the movement glorified violence and imperial greatness, so disarmament is rejected.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The program stresses a strong army and imperial destiny, and the movement valued discipline and will.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Collective organisation of producers in syndicates is central, though under state direction rather than free bargaining.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The program calls for one vertical-syndicate economic order directed by the state.

sacred-nation.rationale: Integral nationalism places the nation as the supreme and enduring community above class and individual.

farm-price-support.rationale: The 1934 program called for agrarian reform and credit support for farmers, with the state organizing producers into syndicates.

workers-own-party.rationale: National syndicalism replaced class parties and parliaments with a vertical syndicate of producers under the state, rejecting separate workers' parties.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The program replaces class unions with vertical syndicates of producers under the state, in which membership is obligatory.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: National syndicalism rejects liberal democracy, parties and parliaments for a state organized by syndicates, so competitive elections do not define legitimacy.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Adherents were split: Redondo was a militant Catholic while Ledesma was an atheist who valued the Church only as a national force.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The program rejects Marxism and class struggle, so a Marxist planned state would not be defended.

indirect-election.rationale: National syndicalism replaces parliaments and parties with a vertical structure of syndicates feeding upward, not direct election.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The program demands a totalitarian unitary state and condemns separatism, so ethnic regional autonomy is rejected.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Integral nationalism treats the nation and its territory as a spiritual unity of destiny, as in the 1934 program.

self-ownership.rationale: The nation-state as a vertical syndicate of producers subordinates the individual to the national whole.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ledesma and the program reject parties and parliaments, although state syndicates remain as the mediating bodies.

national-resource-control.rationale: National syndicalism puts the economy and key resources under the nation-state's direction.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The 1934 program subordinates property to national economic ends through syndicates, nationalized credit and land reform, so process alone does not justify a distribution.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: National syndicalism rejected Marxism, though its Sorelian syndicalist roots honoured the producer, so adherents may have valued labour highly without accepting the Marxist theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Its core aim is to win workers away from Marxist internationalism into a nation organized as a syndicate of producers, so patriotism and serving workers are meant to be one project.

missingStatements.text: The banking and credit system should be nationalized.
missingStatements.rationale: Point 14 of the 1934 program favors nationalizing banking and running major public services through corporations.
Point 6 abolishes parties, inorganic suffrage and conventional parliaments in favor of family, municipal and syndical participation.

missingStatements.text: Large idle or illegitimately held landholdings should be expropriated and redistributed as family farms.
missingStatements.rationale: Points 18, 19 and 21 call for consolidating farms, creating family holdings and expropriating illegitimately held land without compensation.

notes: The Spanish strand is the basis; the Italian strand (Corradini, Rossoni) was more imperialist and openly pro-class-struggle and would answer some items differently. Sources on religion and race are thin, so those answers are low confidence. Ledesma (atheist, pro-union) and José Antonio (Catholic, elitist) differed on religion and labor.
